tour.title: Project Orientation
tour.description: Begin with the project working contract and task-context guide to understand how TingTing is explored, changed, and verified. They provide the operational map for the rest of this tour, so the application architecture is read alongside its delivery constraints.

tour.title: Backend Bootstrap
tour.description: The backend entry module is the natural runtime starting point identified by the topology analysis. It brings the backend application together and leads directly to configuration, persistence, middleware, routes, and operational services introduced in the following steps.

tour.title: Shared Platform Contracts
tour.description: The shared package is a highly depended-on foundation for cross-package calculations, schemas, types, constants, and utilities. Read it before feature code to recognize the common vocabulary and contracts that keep the backend and frontend aligned.

tour.title: Persistence Foundation
tour.description: The database entry module and schema are the two most central nodes in the graph by fan-in, showing that persistent records anchor much of the platform. Together they form the data-access boundary and structural model that business services rely on after the backend starts.

tour.title: Access and HTTP Boundary
tour.description: Authentication middleware protects the request path exposed by the shipment routes. Building on the startup and persistence steps, this pair shows where an authorized logistics request enters the business application before it reaches domain behavior.

tour.title: Shipment Domain Service
tour.description: The shipment service has one of the broadest dependency scopes in the topology, making it a useful lens on the core logistics workflow. It sits after the route boundary and coordinates the persistent and shared foundations needed to implement shipment-domain behavior.

tour.title: Billing Domain Service
tour.description: The billing-document service is the graph's highest fan-out module, so it is a concentrated example of an operational service assembling many supporting concerns. Read it after shipments to see how business workflows extend into financial and document-oriented behavior without losing the shared data model.

tour.title: Frontend Integration Path
tour.description: The frontend API layer and shipment client translate the backend workflow into browser-facing integrations, while the shared UI component module provides reusable presentation building blocks. This connects the service-oriented backend tour to the Vietnamese logistics web client used by role-specific screens.

tour.title: Schema Evolution
tour.description: The baseline migration records the starting persistent structure that complements the schema module from Step 4. It is the right non-code stop for understanding how database changes are ordered and carried forward as logistics capabilities evolve.
tour.languageLesson: Database migrations express incremental schema evolution. Their order matters because later changes assume the persistent structures created by earlier migrations.

tour.title: Local Runtime Environment
tour.description: The development Compose definition describes how the application is run with its supporting services outside the source modules. Ending here connects the code path from backend bootstrap through the frontend and database to the environment that makes the complete platform runnable.
tour.languageLesson: Compose files describe collaborating services as configuration, making local dependencies and their startup relationships explicit instead of embedding them in application code.
